> I think these changes are important, but I have a couple of thoughts:
> 
> 1. `process_last_received_message` passes in just the content to the registered hook method, so it must be a content type (I'm planning to open a PR to define that, but here it is `MessageContentType = Union[str, List[Union[Dict, str]]]`)
> 2. `process_all_messages_before_reply` and `process_message_before_send` can have the same type hint for their hooks, but `process_last_received_message` has a different type for its hooks (see point 1). So annotating `self.hook_lists` might make it difficult to read, so I would be more inclined to not annotate it at all.

Good point, what do you think of this

> I feel ok with your comment but then I'd make a a check on the places where it is used like that to see if is an instance of such type and throw error there. What do you think?

I have a question on the `_num_token_from_messages` function in `token_count_utils.py`.

[Function here](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/c221eea14e0acba569066718bbfeba75fa80aa54/autogen/token_count_utils.py#L87)

How critical is this function for these non-OpenAI client classes? Using the model name here won't always work because the same model could be run from different providers (e.g. Mistral.AI and Together.AI both support 'Mistral' and 'Mixtral' models). Also, Together.AI has a large array of models that can be run.

If we don't handle it, it raises a `NotImplementedError` exception.

So, any suggestions on how to handle this having only the model name? Should we default anything not catered for to gpt-4-0613 as per Gemini?
```
    elif "gemini" in model:
        logger.info("Gemini is not supported in tiktoken. Returning num tokens assuming gpt-4-0613.")
        return _num_token_from_messages(messages, model="gpt-4-0613")
```
author: marklysze

Okay - this is getting close but I have an issue in that I can't get this demo notebook chat to finish. In the notebook, in the last example where it plays chess, how do I have it finish after 4 turns. It has max_turns but I'm not sure if that's in the right place as when I look at the call stack in the code, it just goes between send and receive constantly, not getting back to the main loop and checking max_turns after it enters the loop.

[Here's the notebook file](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/df8f95c0e4a5099d8f32e7c0ebcbe5f6c12fdd26/website/docs/topics/non-openai-models/cloud-togetheraiclient.ipynb)

Code dump is:
```
config_list = [
    {
        # Let's choose Meta's CodeLlama 34b instruct model which supports function calling through the Together.AI API
        "model": "mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1",
        "api_key": os.environ.get("TOGETHER_API_KEY"),
        "api_type": "together",
    }
]

import random

import chess
import chess.svg
from IPython.display import display
from typing_extensions import Annotated

board = chess.Board()


def make_move() -> Annotated[str, "A move in UCI format"]:
    moves = list(board.legal_moves)
    move = random.choice(moves)
    board.push(move)
    # Display the board.
    display(chess.svg.board(board, size=400))
    return str(move)

from autogen import ConversableAgent, register_function

player_white = ConversableAgent(
    name="Player White",
    system_message="You are a chess player and you play as white. " "Always call make_move() to make a move",
    llm_config={"config_list": config_list, "cache_seed": None},
)

player_black = ConversableAgent(
    name="Player Black",
    system_message="You are a chess player and you play as black. " "Always call make_move() to make a move",
    llm_config={"config_list": config_list, "cache_seed": None},
)

board_proxy = ConversableAgent(
    name="Board Proxy",
    llm_config=False,
    # The board proxy will only respond to the make_move function.
    is_termination_msg=lambda msg: "tool_calls" not in msg,
)

register_function(
    make_move,
    caller=player_white,
    executor=board_proxy,
    name="make_move",
    description="Make a move.",
)

register_function(
    make_move,
    caller=player_black,
    executor=board_proxy,
    name="make_move",
    description="Make a move.",
)

player_white.register_nested_chats(
    trigger=player_black,
    chat_queue=[
        {
            "sender": board_proxy,
            "recipient": player_white,
        }
    ],
)

player_black.register_nested_chats(
    trigger=player_white,
    chat_queue=[
        {
            "sender": board_proxy,
            "recipient": player_black,
        }
    ],
)

# Clear the board.
board = chess.Board()

chat_result = player_white.initiate_chat(
    player_black,
    message="Let's play chess! Your move.",
    max_turns=4,
)
```

I thought it may be the termination on the board_proxy but as that's for the nested chat I don't think that affects the main chat.

Any help would be appreciated, perhaps I'm missing something... noting @Hk669, @yiranwu0, @joshkyh, @qingyun-wu

UPDATE - I haven't heard back from Together.AI yet (I put an issue through their repository). I have incorporated the use of the ability to hide tools conditionally and this helps in this scenario and I think will be useful for other scenarios where you just need a tool call made once.

body:
Hey @Hk669, I've tested the Anthropic code and have updated for a few things:
- enforcing alternating roles (must be user, assistant, user, etc.)
- last role can't be assistant (so added a "continue" message at the end)
- updated a few default parameter values as per Anthropic API
- updated the parameter passing so that it uses keyword unpacking instead, as Anthropic doesn't accept `None` values, so any parameter not set can't be set to None.
- Updated the cost so it's calculated upon response creation
- Updated test file, however I think it might be a good idea to have a look through that

Seems to be working with a few tests I did - one a function/tool call, and one just an agent to agent chat. Not extensive by any means. 

Also, I will create a new file "client_utils.py" as per @yiranwu0's suggestion and put the parameter validation into that, so that will end up replacing the `load_config` function. I'll look to do this in the Mistral client.
